title: A Model-Agnostic Approach to Differentially Private Topic Mining

problem.claim: Topic mining can expose users who contributed text data to re-identification threats.

gap.claim: Topic mining requires a privacy-preserving technique that addresses its high sensitivity while maintaining utility.

contributions.claim: TopicDP injects calibrated Gaussian noise into the matrix output of any topic mining algorithm to provide differential privacy and utility.
TopicDP smooths sensitivity for the Gaussian mechanism through sensitivity sampling.
The authors provide theoretical differential privacy guarantees under Rényi differential privacy and utility error bounds for TopicDP.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments were conducted on the Enron email and Amazon Reviews datasets.
The authors report that TopicDP provides better privacy-preserving performance than other differential privacy mechanisms for topic mining.
The authors report that TopicDP is model-agnostic.

narrative_sequence.summary: Topic mining extracts patterns from text data for applications such as intent detection.
Topic mining can create privacy threats through re-identification of text contributors.
TopicDP adds calibrated Gaussian noise to topic-mining matrix outputs and uses sensitivity sampling to address high sensitivity.
The authors establish Rényi differential privacy guarantees and utility error bounds.
Experiments on two real-world text datasets compare TopicDP with other differential privacy mechanisms.

source_observation.claim: Adding calibrated noise to the matrix output of an arbitrary topic mining algorithm is presented as a model-agnostic privacy strategy.

interpretation.claim: A post-processing or output-level privacy layer can potentially decouple privacy protection from the underlying model.

application.claim: When protecting outputs from varied topic mining models, consider an output-level mechanism with explicit sensitivity control.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which topic mining algorithms, privacy budgets, or data conditions are supported.

unknowns: The abstract does not report quantitative utility, privacy, or error-bound values.
The abstract does not describe the experimental protocol, baselines, or statistical significance.
The abstract does not provide implementation or reproducibility details.
